messages.content: Small Phoenix problem: north Scottsdale just added a Friday noon calibration review, and they think it could run until 2:30. My booked PHX-DEN return is late afternoon. Is that too tight?

Yes, tight enough that I would change it if the fare difference is modest. If you leave Scottsdale at 2:45, you still have a 35-50 minute drive to PHX, fuel, rental return, bag/security, and Friday traffic. The current flight works only if the review ends early and nothing goes wrong.
There is a later nonstop Friday around 7:40 for about $80 more. Saturday morning is easy but adds one Tempe hotel night and another day on the rental.

I would rank them: 1) later Friday nonstop: best balance; it gives a real buffer without adding lodging. 2) Saturday morning: least stressful, but harder to justify unless the clinic needs you after 2:30 or weather looks bad. 3) keep the current flight: lowest cost, highest chance of a messy airport run.
Does Tempe still make sense if I move to Saturday?

If you stay until Saturday, Tempe is still acceptable, but it is not adding much value after a north Scottsdale finish. You would mostly be paying to avoid a late Friday flight. If you switch only to the later Friday flight, keep the Tempe hotel as booked and check out Friday morning.
What rental drop-off time should I use for the 7:40?
Set the PHX return for about 5:45 p.m. and attach the new flight number. Plan to fuel near the airport, not in Scottsdale, and leave the clinic by 3:00 if the review ends on time.
Okay, give me the actual order and who needs to hear about it.

Do it in this order: 1) Change PHX-DEN to the 7:40 Friday nonstop and save the fare-difference receipt. Recheck the seat map after ticketing. 2) Keep the Tempe hotel; no extra night needed. 3) Extend the rental return to 5:45 p.m. with the new flight number. 4) Add an expense note that the $80 change avoids an added hotel night, rental day, and meals. 5) Tell north Scottsdale you can stay through 2:30 but need a clean wrap by 3:00. 6) Notify Mesa/Tempe only if materials pickup or shipment timing changes. Put a 2:50 p.m. depart-clinic alert on your calendar.

messages.content: Phoenix is basically done. I need a first plan for the Seattle lab operations summit in late winter. Core sessions are Thursday and Friday in South Lake Union, and there is an optional vendor lab Wednesday afternoon. I am not booking yet, just need the shape.

Good. Two choices drive the plan: whether the Wednesday lab is worth an extra hotel night, and whether Mark might join for the weekend. Are you leaning toward arriving Wednesday, or trying to save the night and fly Thursday morning?
Assume the Wednesday lab is worth attending if I can get there without leaving at dawn. Mark is a maybe for Friday to Sunday. I do not want a rental car unless Seattle makes that foolish.

Then my first cut is Wednesday early-afternoon nonstop DEN-SEA, no rental. It protects Thursday and can reach South Lake Union late afternoon if the vendor lab starts around 4. Thursday morning saves one hotel night, but a delay could put you into the opening session late. Return stays open: Friday evening for work-only, Sunday afternoon if Mark joins.
I see an Alaska nonstop at 12:30 landing about 2:25 and a United one at 1:05 landing about 3:05. The lab starts at 4.

For a 4 p.m. lab, take the 12:30-ish option. The 1:05 is possible only if the lab is drop-in and you can go straight from airport to hotel or badge pickup. The earlier nonstop gives you time for Sea-Tac, traffic, and a quick bag drop without adding a connection.

Hotel options: conference block two blocks away, $249, 4.1 rating. Lake Union hotel is $219, 4.3, quieter, indoor pool and better fitness, no hot tub listed. Boutique waterfront is 4.5 but $310 and farther.

Ranked: 1) Conference block if this is work-only: walkable, fewer logistics, and a solid rating for a short summit stay. 2) Lake Union if you want quieter evenings and better exercise space; lower rate, pool and fitness are stronger, but confirm walk time and accept no listed hot tub. 3) Boutique if Mark joins and waterfront atmosphere matters enough to pay more and ride more.
If Mark comes, I would rather not change hotels Friday. Is Lake Union the better all-through option?

Probably yes, if the walk or short rideshare to sessions is manageable. It gives you a better work stay than the boutique on cost and a better weekend than the block on quiet and amenities. Ask whether the weekend rate stays near $219 and whether pool and fitness hours are usable after sessions.
What about getting from SEA? Light rail to Westlake then rideshare, or just rideshare from the airport?

With a training bag and a tight 4 p.m. lab, rideshare straight to the hotel is the safer arrival move. For the rest, skip the car: walk or rideshare to sessions, rideshare at night, and use transit or ferry options if Mark wants weekend exploring. Rent only for a day trip outside the city.
Would you avoid Thursday morning entirely?

For this plan, yes. Keep it as the budget fallback only. A Thursday morning delay from Denver means you may miss check-in and the opening block, and it removes any chance to settle in. The Wednesday extra hotel night buys reliability.
Draft the plan I can send my director, with decision points.

Proposed plan: fly DEN-SEA Wednesday on the 12:30-ish nonstop, arrive about 2:25, rideshare to South Lake Union, drop bags, and attend the 4 p.m. vendor lab. Hotel: hold Lake Union if Mark is likely and the commute checks out; otherwise use the conference block for the simplest work stay. Transportation: no rental car unless a weekend day trip gets added. Return: Friday evening if solo work-only, or Sunday afternoon if Mark joins. Decide before booking: confirm vendor-lab start and badge process, get approval for the Wednesday hotel night and airport rideshare, get Mark's yes/no date, verify hotel cancellation and weekend rates, confirm the no-hot-tub amenity gap is acceptable, and choose Friday versus Sunday return.
